previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants, type 1 diabetes, and chronic heart failure was admitted for right leg cellulitis and a non-occlusive popliteal vein thrombus. She was started on vancomycin and heparin. During the hospitalization, she developed worsening pulmonary edema and respiratory distress requiring ICU admission and BiPAP support. Her condition improved with hemodialysis and ultrafiltration. She also experienced atrial fibrillation with tachycardia, managed with amiodarone and anticoagulation with warfarin. Repeat imaging showed no DVT, and the final diagnosis was cellulitis without thrombosis. Blood cultures remained negative, and antibiotics were discontinued. She completed a course of meropenem and was transitioned to oral medications. Her immunosuppressants were adjusted, and she was discharged to extended care in stable condition with instructions for CPAP use, daily weight monitoring, and close follow-up.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms ___,
   
You were admitted to the hospital for shortness of breath. You 
were found to have an exacerbation of heart failure because of 
volume overload.  We took off extra fluid during dialysis and 
you felt better.  Because of difficulties with low blood 
pressure during hemodialysis, we feel that you may benefit from 
peritoneal dialysis, where fluid can be taken off over a longer 
period of time. You will likely have a peritoneal catheter 
placed next week.
  
You were started on a new medication Midodrine to help keep your 
blood pressure up during dialysis.
  
Medication Changes
#. START Midodrine 2.5 mg by mouth twice daily (Take on both 
dialysis and non-dialysis days.  Take before dialysis on 
dialysis days.)
#. HOLD Coumadin
  
Because of your heart failure, you should weigh yourself every 
morning, record your daily weights, and call your doctor if your 
weight goes up by more than 3 lbs.
  
It was a pleasure taking care of you during your 
hospitalization.
